title: Tongue & Taste
shortDescription: The four types of papillae on the tongue and how they contribute to taste perception.
genZNote: Helps you taste — four types of tiny bumps doing four different jobs.

illustration.alt: Labelled illustration of the tongue showing the four papillae types
illustration.caption: Tongue (Taste) — Cellfie Human Anatomy

structures.name: Fungiform papillae
structures.description: Mushroom-shaped bumps scattered mostly on the front/sides of the tongue.
structures.function: Contain taste buds; associated with sweet taste.

structures.name: Foliate papillae
structures.description: Ridge-like folds on the sides of the tongue.
structures.function: Contain taste buds; associated with sour taste.

structures.name: Circumvallate papillae
structures.description: Large papillae arranged in a V-shape at the back of the tongue.
structures.function: Contain taste buds; associated with bitter taste.

structures.name: Filiform papillae
structures.description: Thin, cone-shaped papillae covering most of the tongue's surface.
structures.highYield: Filiform papillae generally lack taste buds — they give texture, not taste.

comparisons.distinction: Filiform papillae give mechanical/texture sensation and generally lack taste buds; the other three types all contain taste buds.

questions.prompt: Which type of papillae generally lacks taste buds?
questions.explanation: Filiform papillae provide texture/mechanical sensation and generally lack taste buds, unlike the other three papillae types.
optionNotes: Correct — texture only, generally no taste buds.

questions.prompt: In the labelled tongue illustration, which large, V-shaped papillae sit at the back of the tongue?
questions.explanation: Circumvallate papillae are the large papillae arranged in a V-shape toward the back of the tongue.
optionNotes: Scattered on the front/sides, not V-shaped at the back.

sections.heading: Taste Perception
sections.body: Taste buds, embedded within fungiform, foliate, and circumvallate papillae, contain receptor cells that detect dissolved chemicals from food. Modern physiology recognizes that most taste buds can detect the basic taste qualities (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami) rather than each papillae type being strictly limited to one taste — but the papillae-to-taste associations shown in classic teaching diagrams remain a commonly tested simplification.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The tongue's papillae house taste buds (except filiform papillae, which are purely textural) that detect dissolved food chemicals as taste.
keyFacts: Filiform papillae have no taste buds — their role is purely mechanical/textural.
Circumvallate papillae are the largest and sit at the back of the tongue in a V-shaped row.
Fungiform, foliate, and circumvallate papillae all contain taste buds.
commonConfusion: Filiform papillae are the one type without taste buds — a frequently tested exception among the four papillae types.

highYieldFacts: Filiform papillae provide texture/grip, not taste — the only papillae type without taste buds.
commonTraps: Don't assume all four papillae types detect taste — filiform papillae do not.
mustRemember: Four papillae types: fungiform, foliate, circumvallate, filiform (texture only, no taste buds).
